thread:
incident-bot: [AUTO-PAGER] SEV2 gpu-prefill-oom on cluster-prod-7 (2921112222) -> paging oncall

mike: Got the page. Noting container restarts on gpu-node-23 while processing long-context prefill for model `redwood/llm-xl-4k`. Logs show SIGTERM after CUDA OOM. @sara @kai can you triage?

sara: Looking into pod logs. Repro snippet shows huge KV cache alloc during prefill; runtime raised CUDA OOM then process was killed.

kai: Confirming at node level: GPU mem at 99-100% for sustained period, dmesg has oom_kill entries for the runtime pid. Sample from kube logs:
```
[2026-04-02T11:03:47Z] runtime ERROR: CUDA error: out of memory
[2026-04-02T11:03:47Z] kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 7543 (redwood-runtime)
```

jess: Support flagged two customers (acct-omega, acct-delta) with streaming disconnects and transient 5xx around the same time. They're asking if this will recur.

mike: Early impact estimate: ~3% of /v1/generate requests returned 5xx for large-context customers on that pool. Immediate actions: isolate node and throttle huge prefill.

sara: Executing isolation now:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-23
kubectl drain gpu-node-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=30
```

kai: Also pushing a short-lived runtime backpressure flag to increase prefill headroom for the pool: `prefill.kv_headroom_percent` 5 -> 30 via rollout flag. Submitting change.

incident-bot: Change queued: featureflag(prefill.kv_headroom_percent)=30 by kai (chg-6791) - starting rollout

ops-bot: Gateway rule proposal: reject prefill requests > 12000 tokens with 429 + header `x-prefill-blocked: true`. Will return link to best-practices doc.

mike: Throttling at gateway sounds good. Implement the reject response and include a suggestion to use streaming + smaller prefill or model-window fallback.

kai: Gateway rule applied. Example enforcement behavior: 429 body: {"error":"prefill too large"}, header `x-prefill-blocked: true`. Rolling out to edge in 30s.

jess: Notified acct-omega and acct-delta of temporary mitigation and recommended workarounds; they acknowledge and are testing reduced context.

sara: After cordon + headroom flag + gateway cap we see immediate reduction in GPU memory spikes. No new oom_kill entries in last 10m and restarts stopped.

mike: Root cause summary for handoff: oversized prefill long-context requests led to KV cache allocation spike and CUDA OOM causing SIGTERM/restarts. Mitigations applied: cordon/drain of offending node, increase runtime prefill headroom, gateway prefill token cap, customer communications.

kai: Follow-ups I will open:
- ENG-RUNTIME: investigate graceful KV spill-to-host and more aggressive prefill backpressure.
- ENG-ML: examine model kv allocation behavior and recommend quantized KV format where safe.
- PLAT: add per-tenant prefilling quotas and better noisy-neighbor detection.

I'll open PM-2921112222-prefill-node23 as the postmortem draft.

sara: I'll monitor the pool for 45m then prepare rollback plan for the headroom flag if no regressions. :thumbsup:

jess: I'll keep Support updated and send a customer follow-up once the postmortem link is available.

mike: Good work all. Closing pager when monitoring window ends. Ping oncall if any recurrence.
